body.statement:
For the switching incidence sets and protocol weights,
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
   \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when no cover exists.  Writing \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(M=|\Omega|\), the complete incidence relation is constructible with at most \(2^m\) distinct source-oracle queries and \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) work, because \(M\leq k2^L\).  Branch-mask dynamic programming or protocol-subset enumeration then computes the exact optimum in
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
\]
time.  Weighted greedy on this explicit protocol-to-branch incidence returns an accepted certificate of cost at most \(H_M\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\), where \(H_M=\sum_{r=1}^{M}r^{-1}\), in \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) time whenever the instance is feasible.  This is a protocol-cover guarantee after incidence enumeration, not a polynomial-time action-cover guarantee.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal P(E)\) be the distinct protocols occurring in the nonempty records of an accepted sparse certificate.  Each branch \(\alpha\) occurs in exactly one such record, and that record passes the predicate \(\mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}\).  Hence
\[
 \Omega\subseteq\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S).
 \tag{9}
\]
The reverse inclusion is automatic because each incidence set is a subset of \(\Omega\), so \(\mathcal P(E)\) is a cover.  Removing index-zero markers can only lower cost, and therefore
\[
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}w(S)\leq\operatorname{Cost}(E).
 \tag{10}
\]

Conversely, let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\) cover \(\Omega\).  For every branch \(\alpha\), choose the first \(S\in\mathcal P\) with \(\alpha\in K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\), and then choose the first witness \((\ell,T,\tau)\) in the existential definition of that incidence.  Make one singleton-index record for \(\alpha\).  Every local check holds by \(\mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}=1\), and every branch is represented exactly once.  Each branch has a successful source in the decoded complete collection, so the full operational run returns nonfailure and \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}=1\).  Omitting protocols of \(\mathcal P\) unused by these records can only lower the nonnegative cost.  Taking minima in the two directions (9)--(10) proves
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\cup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
   \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
 \tag{11}
\]
This equality is derived from operational acceptance and distinct-protocol charging; it is not a definition of the causal query.

We next construct every incidence bit.  Enumerate the \(2^m\) protocol masks.  Catalogue scans check SELECT cardinality, mechanism use, precedence, and conflicts, while the published CTF-REALIZE runtime lemma checks physical compatibility in polynomial time.  Query each legal mask at most once and cache its immutable reply.  For a non-\(\bot\) reply enumerate the \(2^L\) literal masks, reject inconsistent labels, and use the returned support table to test the event actually conditioned upon.  From each surviving slice, the canonical ancestral and district decomposition lists at most \(n\) single-district factors.  Measured ancestry is a graph-and-action check.

For a factor \(C_j\), suppose its free request positions have domain sizes \(h_1,\ldots,h_r\).  The equality type is induced by the assignment and supplies no extra independent choice.  Since the literal table contains one request literal for each possible value,
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{u=1}^{r}h_u
 \leq2^{\sum_{u=1}^{r}h_u}
 \leq2^L,
 \qquad
 M=\sum_{j=1}^{k}|\Omega_j|\leq k2^L.
 \tag{12}
\]
For every enumerated \(\alpha,S,\ell,T\), instantiate the value matches and run the ancestor--district recursion.  Proposition~\(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) decides failure, and Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) supplies the canonical transcript on success.  Therefore all and only the true incidence bits are recorded.  The number of branch checks is at most
\[
 2^m2^L nM
 \leq 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).
 \tag{13}
\]
Reading the exact support replies contributes their actual total length \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  Thus (13), including graph work and exact cost arithmetic, is
\[
 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}),
 \tag{14}
\]
and uses no more than \(2^m\) distinct oracle queries.  Notice that zero-mass unused cells are merely table entries; no division by them occurs.

List the protocols with nonempty incidence as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\leq2^m\).  For \(U\subseteq\Omega\), initialize \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for \(U\ne\varnothing\), and set
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\{D_{i-1}(U),D_{i-1}(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i))+w(S_i)\}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Induction on \(i\) shows that \(D_i(U)\) is the least weight of a subcollection of the first \(i\) protocols covering \(U\): an optimum either omits \(S_i\), or includes it and leaves \(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i)\).  Thus (15) evaluates (11) in \(O(p2^M)\) arithmetic operations.  Alternatively, enumerate the \(2^p\) protocol subsets and test their unions.  Choosing the faster alternative and adding (14) gives
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}).
 \tag{16}
\]

Finally consider the weighted greedy algorithm recorded in the published weighted-greedy lemma.  We derive the exact constant needed here.  First take every zero-cost protocol that covers a new branch.  Thereafter, when \(r\) branches remain, an optimum cover of cost \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) covers those branches, so summing newly covered branch counts over its protocols is at least \(r\).  Hence some optimum protocol has ratio at most \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}/r\) between its cost and its number of newly covered branches.  Greedy chooses no larger a ratio.  Charge that ratio to each branch newly covered in the step.  As \(r\) decreases from \(M\) to \(1\), the total charge, which equals greedy cost, is at most
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\sum_{r=1}^{M}\frac1r
 =H_M\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}.
 \tag{17}
\]
If the optimum is zero, the initial zero-cost phase covers every branch and (17) still holds.  The cover-to-certificate construction above yields an accepted sparse certificate.  Greedy is polynomial in the explicit incidence size, so (14) is its total construction time.  This proves every assertion.
body.justification: The theorem identifies the exact finite protocol-cover optimization induced by operational acceptance.
body.gap: Certificate-string enumeration obscured the smaller branch-mask or protocol-subset state space.
body.consumer: It supplies the exact runtime, infeasibility obstruction, and \(H_M\) benchmark.
